correctness.rationale: Let norm-one T:X→Y=(⊕Fγ)_ℓ1, all Fγ finite dimensional; choose x_n∈S_X with ||Tx_n||→1. Union of countable supports of Tx_n is countable; diagonal compactness gives coordinatewise block-norm limit u∈Y with t=||u||≤1 (Fatou). A gliding-hump subsequence splits Tx_{n_j}=u+b_j+o_Y(1) with pairwise disjoint finite block supports and ||b_j||→1−t because the u-mass on those supports vanishes. The free-ultrafilter ξ=w*-lim J_X x_{n_j} has ||ξ||≤1, T**ξ=J_Yu+w*-lim J_Yb_j. For any ε>0 pick a finite H supporting ≥t−ε of u and ONE functional fε in unit Y* simultaneously supporting u on H and each sufficiently late b_j on their disjoint blocks. Thus Re(T**ξ)(fε)≥1−2ε and ||T**ξ||=||T||=1, which forces ||ξ||=1. Works for arbitrary nonseparable X/Γ and real or complex scalars via Re. Infinite-dimensional blocks genuinely excluded: Hilbert diagonal T e_n=(n/(n+1))e_n fails second-adjoint norm attainment. The disjoint-support geometry and finite-block compactness yield a reusable boundary for second-adjoint norm attainment, while infinite-dimensional block counterexample shows genuine dependence on the hypothesis.
